item.title: Vedanta seeks premium over imported LNG prices for Rajasthan gas sale
item.description: Vedanta Oil and Gas Ltd is seeking a premium over imported LNG prices for 1.80 million standard cubic metres per day (mmscmd) of natural gas from its Rajasthan block, putting the volume up for sale through an electronic auction. The three-month supply contract, running from January 1 to April 1, 2027, will be auctioned on December 14, according to a request for proposal dated November 20 and a draft gas sales agreement. Bidders have been asked to quote a premium they are willing to pay over the monthly average of Platts West India spot liquefied natural gas (LNG) prices, with the highest bids receiving priority in the allocation of available volumes. The starting premium is zero, with bids required to increase in increments of at least USD 0.05 per million British thermal units (MMBtu), according to the tender document. item.title: Adani Group planning $120 bn in capex over next 5-6 years: Jefferies
item.description: Adani Group plans to invest more than USD 120 billion over the next five to six years across infrastructure, energy and data centres while seeking to keep net debt below 3.5 times earnings (EBITDA), according to a Jefferies research note on the group's annual conference. The group is leaning on its financial record as it expands in power, ports, transmission and data centres. At its annual investor conference, the group said its net debt-to-EBITDA ratio had declined from a peak of around 3.6-3.8 times during 2019-23. Group Chief Financial Officer Jugeshinder Singh highlighted lower borrowing costs, improving asset returns and a diversified funding base as evidence of stronger financial resilience, according to a Jefferies research note on the event. However, Jefferies' forecasts for six listed Adani companies put their aggregate net debt-to-EBITDA ratio at 3.7 times in FY27 and FY28, before declining to 3.4 times in FY29 and 3.1 times in FY30. item.title: Tata Sons board meet postponed to Nov 30 after Noel raises concerns
item.description: Tata Sons on Monday postponed a crucial board meeting which was set to discuss the way ahead on the listing of the holding company of the country's largest conglomerate by four days to November 30. The postponement has been necessitated after a letter from Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata on Sunday raising concerns about the mandatory seven-day notice period for a board meeting not being followed, as the agenda was put up only four days in advance. The agenda for the meeting has not been changed, and it is only the day which has been postponed to November 30 from November 26 earlier to give sufficient time for all the directors to prepare for the meeting, as per people in the know. The crucial meeting on November 30 will discuss items including RBI-mandated listing of Tata Sons or ways ahead on complying with the central bank's requests, they said. Divisions among the top echelons on the way ahead for the group had come into the open at the last board meet of Tata Sons on September 1

item.title: Tata Projects bags order for 1,600 MW thermal power plant in Central India
item.description: EPC major Tata Projects Ltd (TPL) on Monday said it has secured an order to build the complete supporting setup for a 1,600 MW coal-fired power plant in Central India. Under the contract, Tata Projects will be responsible for the design, engineering, manufacture, supply, construction, erection, testing, and commissioning of the project's balance-of-plant systems. These systems encompass critical infrastructure required to support reliable plant operations beyond the boiler-turbine-generator island, the company said in a statement. "Tata Projects Ltd (TPL), one of India's leading Engineering, Procurement and Construction (EPC) companies, has been awarded the complete Balance of Plant (BoP) turnkey package for a 2 x 800 MW ultra-supercritical thermal power project in Central India by a leading integrated power utility," the statement said. The project encompasses the complete BoP scope, including coal and biomass handling systems, fuel and ash management facilities, water intake, ..

item.title: Attero to invest ₹3,000 cr to expand critical mineral extraction capacity
item.description: E-waste recycling company Attero plans to invest Rs 3,000 crore in the next five years to scale up its critical mineral extraction capacity, a top official of the company said. Attero Co-founder and CEO Nitin Gupta told PTI that the company plans to enhance total e-waste recycling capacity by over four times to 1 million tonnes in the next four years. "We are specifically looking to invest around Rs 3,000 crore in critical minerals facility expansion over the next five years. Roughly 40 per cent of that will go towards lithium, nickel, and if you read the scheme, within nickel, they have said they considered cobalt as well," he said. Attero claims to extract over 22 critical minerals, including gold, silver, copper, aluminum, nickel, lithium, cobalt and rare earths like neodymium, dysprosium, etc. "Our current capacity for electronic waste recycling is around 2,25,000 tonnes per annum.
